name: Driverr: SSH for Agents
subtitle: Keep an eye on herdr sessions
description:
Driverr is a free, native SSH client for iPhone and iPad, built around herdr — the terminal workspace manager that keeps coding agents running in persistent background terminals.

Most terminal apps treat herdr as one more TUI to render. Driverr treats it as what it is: a remote object model. Workspaces, tabs, panes and agents are real screens, not characters on a grid, and the terminal is one view among several rather than the only one.

The specific thing Driverr does better than a general-purpose SSH client is tell you, on a phone, that an agent is waiting on you — and let you answer it without reading a terminal.

• NEEDS YOU — every blocked agent, collected at the top of the session, named with the workspace and tab it came from. The answer to "is anything waiting on me?" is the first thing on screen.

• REPLY WITHOUT A TERMINAL — a Claude Code or Codex conversation shows as a chat. Type a reply in the composer below it, or attach an image. When the agent asks a question that has options, tap a reply chip under the question. For a permission prompt, the chips are Approve and Deny.

• A REAL TERMINAL WHEN YOU WANT ONE — attach to any pane, with a key row for the characters iOS hides, and themes and type sizes you can change while looking at it.

• PANE CONTROLS — rename or close a pane from the toolbar, and open a new one from the pane switcher.

• KEYS AND PASSWORDS — generate or import an Ed25519 key, or use a password. Both live in the device Keychain.

• HOST KEYS CHECKED — Driverr remembers a host's key the first time it sees it and stops hard if it ever changes.

Driverr has no backend. It talks directly to your own machines over SSH, and nothing about your hosts, keys or sessions goes anywhere else.

Free, and open source.

Driverr is an independent project and is not affiliated with herdr, Anthropic or OpenAI.
promotionalText: See which coding agent is blocked, answer it in two taps, and get on with your day — without reading a full terminal on a phone screen.
reviewNotes:
Driverr is an SSH client. To review it fully you need a machine you can SSH into; a
Mac with Remote Login enabled in Sharing works.

Without a host to connect to, the app still shows: the host list and add-host form,
key generation and import, and the settings screen.

Driverr has no account and no backend, so there is nothing to sign in to and no demo
credentials to provide.
